newsitem.title: INDIA: Former Kashmir legislator shot dead by guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Former Kashmir legislator shot dead by guerrillas.

text.p: A former legislator of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state was shot dead on Monday by unidentified militants, police said.
They said militants shot dead Ghulam Rasool Bhat and his brother-in-law Ghulam Nabi Lone near a bus-stop at Nowpora village in the apple-growing town of Sopore.
The killings occurred some 50 km (30 miles) north of Srinagar, summer capital of the Himalayan state.
Bhat was a former legislator and member of Jammu and Kashmir's ruling National Conference party. No militant group has claimed responsibility for the killings.
In a separate incident, at least three people and a soldier were killed in a mine blast on Sunday night in the state's Anantnag district, the United News of India said.

Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in Kashmir since a separatist revolt broke out in 1990. More than a dozen former legislators have been killed during the seven-year-old rebellion.
